title: Bootstrapping Helm/Node: install failures & quick probes
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes for recurring bootstrapping failures when provisioning new k8s nodes and running Helm installs during cluster bring-up. This is a scratchpad — fragments, commands tried, error dumps, hypotheses, and next small experiments. Keep short, actionable steps to reproduce / triage during on-call.

Symptoms seen (summary):
- Node boots but stays NotReady (Ready=Unknown / NotReady) for >5m.
- Pods stuck in ContainerCreating or CrashLoopBackOff immediately after helm install (CNI or mount errors).
- Helm install times out (ERR: "context deadline exceeded" or chart hooks failing).
- Kubelet logs show: "failed to run pod sandbox" or "cni plugin not found" or "failed to create sandbox: permission denied".

Immediate checks (one-liners I run first):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl describe node $NODE | sed -n '1,200p'
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80
- sudo systemctl status containerd --no-pager
- sudo journalctl -u cloud-init -n 200 | sed -n '1,200p'
- ip link show | egrep 'cni|flannel|weave|calico'
- ls -la /etc/cni/net.d || true

Commands & snippets I've used and why:
1) Check kubelet bootstrap/kubeadm join issues:
   sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 | grep -i "bootstrap" -i
   Look for tls bootstrap / certificate signing errors. If kubelet can't get cert from control plane, node remains NotReady.

2) CNI problems (common):
   # if /etc/cni/net.d missing, CNI plugin not loaded\   ls -la /etc/cni/net.d\   sudo ctr -n k8s.io images ls | head -n 30   # ensure image pulled for cni (e.g., calico, canal)
   kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep 'calico|flannel|weave|cilium|kube-proxy'

3) Container runtime mismatch / cgroup driver mismatch:
   # containerd uses systemd cgroup. kubelet may be configured otherwise.
   sudo cat /etc/containerd/config.toml | sed -n '1,120p'
   sudo systemctl show --property=Environment kubelet
   # if mismatch, set kubelet cgroup driver to systemd in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml or use kubeadm flags.

4) Volume attach / ephemeral disk issues (seen on cloud VMs):
   dmesg | egrep -i 'scsi|nvme|xvd|sd' | tail -n 60\   lsblk -f\   mount | egrep '/var/lib/kubelet|/var/lib/docker|/var/lib/containerd'
   # If ephemeral device delayed, kubelet may fail to prepare volumes; look for mount errors in pod describe.

Typical error snippets I copy into jira Slack to give context:
- kubelet: "Failed create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up sandbox container \"...\": networkPlugin cni failed to set up pod \"...\" network: No such file or directory"
- kubelet: "containerd: container not started: container status: unknown"
- cloud-init: "cloud-init[xyz] ERROR: datasource did not return" (signals metadata timing issues)

Hypotheses I chase (ordered by likelihood I've seen):
1) CNI install didn't finish / Image pull fails during helm chart preflight. Fix: re-run daemonset pods, check imagePullErrors (kubectl describe ds).
2) Node's network namespace / iptables not configured because of missing kernel modules (br_netfilter) or sysctl values. Check: 
   sudo lsmod | grep br_netfilter\   sudo sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables
   If false, apply: sudo modprobe br_netfilter; sudo sysctl -w net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1
3) Container runtime isn't ready (containerd crashed). Check logs and restart containerd + kubelet.
   sudo systemctl restart containerd kubelet; watch journalctl -f -u kubelet
4) Time skew / cert issues: if node clock off, TLS bootstrap fails. Check: date; timedatectl

Small experiments I try (fast, low-risk):
- sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sleep 30 && kubectl get nodes\- If transient, node comes Ready quickly.
- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep ImagePullBackOff (if CNI pods missing images)\- docker/ctr pull the image on node manually to see network/proxy problem.
- scp kubelet log to laptop: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 1000 --no-pager > /tmp/kubelet.log && scp /tmp/kubelet.log me@laptop:/tmp

Helm-specific notes (when chart install fails during bootstrap):
- Helm hooks are executed as jobs/ pods. If cluster scheduling still broken, hook jobs time out and chart is marked FAILED.
- helm install timeout defaults are often too short in slow bootstrapping clusters. Use --timeout 10m and --wait to let CNI/CRDs finish.
- Example: helm install --wait --timeout 10m0s my-cni ./charts/cni --debug
- If helm is failing with "context deadline exceeded" and logs show "X reason: node(s) not ready", the correct fix is to resolve node readiness, not rerun helm repeatedly.

Quick build of a reproducible checklist (for pagers):
1) Confirm node sees API server: curl -k https://$APISERVER:6443/healthz\2) kubelet logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200; search for 'error', 'failed', 'runtimes'\3) Check container runtime status and logs (containerd / docker)\4) Ensure /etc/cni/net.d exists & contains config files\5) Check kube-system pods - especially kube-proxy and CNI pods\6) Check node system resources: free -h; df -h /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/kubelet\7) Check cloud-init or cloud-provider logs for disk attach issues\8) If suspect TLS: check /var/lib/kubelet/pki and kubelet bootstrap logs

Notes from a recent incident (2025-02-10):
- Sequence: new worker VM spun in GCP -> kubeadm join ran via cloud-init -> kubelet attempted TLS bootstrap -> kubelet kept retrying with "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" -> control-plane certs were rotated earlier same day (RED-1234) -> Node never completed cert signing.
- Temporary mitigation: manually copy /etc/kubernetes/pki from a control-plane node to new node (unsafe, ephemeral) to get into cluster for debugging. Permanent fix: ensure CA rotation completed and the CA bundle in the signing controller updated.
- Reason: control-plane had an automated cert-rotation job that cleared the old signing CSRs (bad automation). Created Jira RED-1234.

Leftover TODOs / experiments to add to runbook:
- Add a small utility script: /usr/local/bin/k8s-quick-check.sh that runs the immediate checks above and prints a short report.
- Add kubelet verbose logging flag in cloud-init (KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--v=4) for faster triage during autoscaling waves.
- Add helm chart preflight probe to block installs until kube-system CNI pods are Ready.

Useful one-liners to copy next time:
- kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | [ .metadata.name, .status.conditions[] | select(.type=="Ready") | .status ] | @tsv'\- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep 'calico|cilium|weave|flannel|kube-proxy'\- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 | sed -n '1,200p' | egrep -i 'error|failed|panic'

References / links
- Incident: JIRA RED-1234 (bootstrap TLS failures)
- PR that changed CA rotation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789
- Slack thread (select): #infra on 2025-02-10 -> message id: thread/abc123 (copy upstream)

Bottom line: 80% of bootstrap failures I've seen reduce to (a) missing/slow CNI pods (image pull, private registry auth), (b) runtime not healthy (containerd crashed or cgroup mismatch), or (c) TLS/bootstrap signing race during CA rotation. Keep short checks handy, avoid rerunning helm until the cluster reports node Ready.

Quick save log: captured snippet (paste when creating Jira):
"Feb 10 14:02:11 startup kubelet[1234]: E0210 14:02:11.123456    1234 kubelet.go:2121] Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up sandbox container \"...\": networkPlugin cni failed to set up pod \"metrics-server-...\": no such file or directory"
